title: Valid Parentheses
hints: Use a stack to remember opening brackets that have not been matched.
Each closing bracket must match the most recent opening bracket, and the stack must be empty at the end.
description: Given a string s containing just the characters '(', ')', '{', '}', '[' and ']', determine if the input string is valid. An input string is valid when every opening bracket is closed by the same type of bracket and brackets are closed in the correct order.
constraints: s consists only of parentheses, brackets, and braces

examples.explanation: The pair of parentheses is correctly closed.

title: Binary Search
hints: Keep a search interval and compare the target with its midpoint.
After each comparison, discard the half that cannot contain the target.
description: Given an array of integers nums which is sorted in ascending order, and an integer target, write a function to search for target in nums. If target exists, return its index; otherwise, return -1.
constraints: All integers in nums are unique
nums is sorted in ascending order

title: Valid Anagram
hints: Anagrams have the same character counts.
Sorting both strings is a simple way to compare their character multisets.
description: Given two strings s and t, return true if t is an anagram of s, and false otherwise. An anagram is a word or phrase formed by rearranging the letters of a different word or phrase.
constraints: s and t consist of lowercase English letters

title: Maximum Subarray
hints: Track the best sum of a subarray ending at the current position.
Also track the best sum seen overall so all-negative inputs work correctly.
description: Given an integer array nums, find the subarray with the largest sum, and return its sum. A subarray is a contiguous non-empty sequence of elements within an array.

examples.explanation: The subarray [4, -1, 2, 1] has the largest sum.

title: Subsets
hints: For each number, choose whether it belongs in the current subset.
Backtrack by adding the current subset before exploring the next number.
description: Given an integer array nums of unique elements, return every possible subset (the power set). The order of the subsets does not matter; keep the elements within each subset in input order.
constraints: All values in nums are unique

examples.explanation: There are 2^3 = 8 subsets. Their order in the output is arbitrary.

title: Two Sum
hints: For each number, look for its complement: target minus the current value.
Store values you've already seen in a hash map so each lookup is constant time.
description: Given an array of integers nums and an integer target, return the indices of the two numbers that add up to target. Each input has exactly one solution, and you may not use the same element twice.
